steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Arrange ancho chiles on a baking sheet. Bake in the preheated oven until toasted 3 to 4 minutes.
Remove and discard stems and seeds from toasted peppers. Place peppers in a bowl; add enough hot water to bowl until peppers completely covered. Soak for 1 hour.

Combine ancho chiles, about 1 cup broth, tomato paste, oil, garlic, salt, oregano, and cumin in a blender; blend until smooth. Combine ancho chile mixture and remaining 2 cups beef broth in a saucepan over medium heat; simmer until heated through, about 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: The Best Red Enchilada Sauce
raw_recipe.description: This smoky and savory red enchilada sauce recipe uses dried Ancho chiles, garlic, oregano, and cumin in a beef broth and tomato paste base. It's the best.
raw_recipe.name: The Best Red Enchilada Sauce

review.reviewBody:
New Mexico and California chilies work too. Look for LARGE dark red dried chilies **To save time, after roasting and cleaning the seeds out, lightly simmer the chilies for 20-30min in the broth. Once soft add the chilies and the broth you cooked them in to the blender and add 1/4-1/2 cup more broth to compensate for some cooking off. AllRecipes won't let me update the recipe to say this I'm sorry!! ****If you read the reviews you'll see those who stuck with the recipe as is gave it a high rating, those who tweaked it first with other options gave it a lower rating... My rule of thumb for ALL recipes is to try it how it's written first (unless I am simply SURE there is some ingredient I don't like). Once I try a recipe as written, then I will almost always tweak it the following times I make it. I don't think it's fair to change the recipe as written and then give it a poor review... Try my rule of thumb and make it 'as written' the first time before tweaking it, you will probably still tweak it to your liking, but probably in a totally different way than you expected.********

To the reviewer that had bitter sauce: that happens sometimes if the chilies get roasted too much, it only takes 30 seconds of over doing it to over roast the chilies. If you try again watch them VERY closely, they should just start to smell nice, the color really should not darken and if they look black at ALL then they are over roasted and will make a bad bitter sauce... done it too! Love, Christine

I made this last night! It was so easy and so flavorful. I've roasted dried chilies before so I knew to watch them carefully. If you over-roast the skin will become crispy and bitter, which will translate to the finished sauce. I actually roast the chilies in my toaster oven on 300 degrees, turning frequently. This does a good job softening up the chilies and they puff up and become fragrant. 

Changes: I added a cup of hot broth to the soaking liquid and used the soaking liquid to puree the chilies and other ingredients. I used olive oil instead of corn oil. Not sure how it changed the flavor since I didn't do a side-by-side comparison, but my husband really liked the sauce so yay for me. I like my red sauce a little spicy and knew that the ancho chilies I used were very mild, so I used some red pepper flakes in the puree to kick it up a notch. I will definitely make this again.

loved this sauce. so easy. thick and rich, like a mole. for recipe consistency I just went with the whole 2 oz bag of ancho chili pods. I swapped olive oil for veg oil and used chicken broth. I toast my anchos stove top in a cast iron pan, that way I can keep a better eye on them, and I wasn't gonna heat up the whole oven for it to only be needed for a few minutes. I also seed and stem them before toasting when they are more pliable. I have tried New Mexico, ancho and guajillo chile pods. I like the guajillo flavor the best.

Sorry - I had to modify it at the outset for some vegan/vegetarian family members.
Instead of beef broth, I made a simple vegetable broth by simmering 4 C water with 1/2 tsp salt, a carrot, a quartered onion, and a stick of celery. I let it simmer until the peppers were done soaking, and then used 3 cups of the broth.
I also prepared the soaked chilies by processing them with a little of the broth in my processor with an 's' blade, since my blender isn't that great. This makes a beautiful, smooth, delicious paste of the peppers that had me salivating well before my enchiladas were done!
Other than not using the beef broth, I really made it as written, and it was superb. Thank you so much for this recipe.

I've made this a few times now and my spoiled So Cal family loves this recipe. You absolutely cannot over roast the chilis! Stop when they become fragrant and a bit soft otherwise you'll have bitter sauce. I've started improvising and found that a small amount of cinnamon (1/4 t) and sugar (2 t) as well as a bit more salt are great additions. I also strain and reduce the sauce after. Excellent recipe.

Just made this sauce incorporating Fox Woadhill Rogers's edit of simmering the chilies for 25 minutes before blending. To be accurate, I used veggie broth (vegetarians in the family) and avocado oil instead of corn oil. My taste test confirms that it is amazing! -- Elisa

I normally don't care for red enchilada sauce, and favor green instead. But this sauce is really great! I LOVED how this recipe wasn't tomato heavy! The beef broth works perfectly with all the chili flavors, and the seasoning is spot-on!

After reading some of the reviews I got scared of burning the peppers, so i toasted them @350 for 3 min. I noticed that they darkened up a little bit, but definitely didn't turn black. Might be hard to tell if you burned them because the ancho chilies are already super dark, almost black already. 

I used 1 huge ancho, and 5 california chilies. Instead of covering the chilies with water, I used 2 cups of beef broth, and simmered them for 20-30 min. They really soaked up a lot of liquid, so I ended up still adding 2 more cups of broth. So total I used 4 cups broth, which happens to be an entire carton of beef broth. (perfect!) Once I got to blending everything, I also added one chipotle chili with a bit of adobo (from a can.) I didn't to that for heat, just to diversify the chili flavors. 

I added a little bit (1/4 cup) of caramelized onions to the blender, not that the recipe needed it. I just happen to be obsessed with onions, and can't seem to eat a meal without them.

My Mexican mother in law never roasted the chilis, she cooked them in the broth until they were soft (she taught me this method for pesole). She then took out the seeds and pulp and whirred the peppers in the blender with the stock. After that, she strained it to get out the skins. It works really well and reduces the bitterness. It is also not that time consuming.

That being said, I did roast the chilis for a few minutes, and I liked the boost of flavor that the roasting provided. I also rubbed just a bit of olive oil on the chilis prior to roasting. Loved the hint from another cook to heat the chilis on the stovetop instead, I might try that next time.

I thought that the salt was just right, I don't tend to use too much salt. The only other thing I added was a bit of dried basil and a little minced onion (personal preference). I would have given this five stars, but I thought that the method of preparing the chilis was off just a little. I'd really say 4.5 stars.

I wanted to add, I really love the opportunity to look at these recipes and then experiment based on others' experience and my family's preferences. We all have different tastes!

Thanks for the recipe! It is a good one.

I followed the recipe with the exception of using 7 Pasilla Chili Pods since it was all I had. This turned out quite well. I also simmered the chilis for 30 minutes in vegetable broth since it was all I had on hand. After the blend, I simmered it for about 15 minutes and it was delicious. Better than sauces made with spices alone.

This is the best recipe for homemade enchilada sauce I have ever made. Very simple but effective. I did the simmer on a very low heat for 45 minutes and it really brought out the flavors from the chilies. I also used a strong beef stock. Basically i would not change anything.

Hi Christine! Your sauce is lovely though I never use recipes other than as guidelines. Two largely ignored secrets of nearly every savoury Mexican sauce I make are cumin (which I use much more of) and the truly obscure and astounding addition of ground clove - maybe more than a tablsp or so. Then I use (or overuse) much more garlic, oregano, chile (the sweet sort; don't want to cause riots among non-Mexican taste buds, do we?) and slightly less oil. Grind your dry spices in a small coffee grinder and you approach Montezuman stature! As to roasted peppers, you can achieve the same results by drying out some of the varieties that come in jars and dry pan-roasting them until they are brittle. Then into your handy-dandy grinder they go! With love of food, David Peevers
Delicious sauce. I made chicken enchiladas, these were excellent!!!
A great sauce for enchiladas. A bit too strong for kids so thin with 2 cans of store enchilada sauce.
Great flavors. I added some smoked paprika to mine.
End result had just a hint of an almost vinegar taste. I added more cumin and ground clove to taste and it was perfect! Better the next day as flavors came together.

This sauce has great flavour and the heat is real! I thought it was a bit thin so I boiled it down a bit. I did substitute a can of chipotle chiles in adobo sauce as ancho chili are difficult to find in my area of Canada. But I didn't have to worry about the roasting so that saves time!
Added this sauce to my chicken enchilada soup. This soup has a nice smokey warm flavor. Looking forward to using the extra sauce in other recipes.
I made this three times following the recipe to the letter. It’s not a sauce…it’s a burnt tasting crust. Canned enchilada sauce from a grocery store is better than this.

This recipe (followed exactly) was a bit bitter and too thick so I added some sugar (about 1 Tbs), 6 oz of tomato sauce and about 1/4 C vodka. After using it on beef enchiladas, I still think it needs a more tomatoey flavor, so I added another cup of tomato sauce and simmered it for another 10 minutes. YUM
